There used to be an old fisherman who wove his own bamboo baskets with patient hands. He never left for the deep waters without checking if his family had enough rice for the morning. Something he carried still rests nearby.

I remember someone who knew the ocean's moods better than anyone... He didn't fish for pride, but to put fish on his family's plate and help neighbors who had none. Look around—a weaver's basket was left by the sand.
An old friend used to say: 'A sturdy basket holds more than fish—it carries a father's promise.' Look near the shore edge; a memory fragment has taken shape.
The sea took his boat, but it couldn't wash away his honest labor. I can almost see his woven fish basket resting in the light nearby.
Before the dark storm, there was an old father repairing his bamboo traps right here. He always shared his extra catch with widows in the barangay. Search close by—his memory lingers.
